Welcome to Bordon Junior School, where every child can be happy and successful. We know every child is unique and we value the energy and enthusiasm they bring to our community of learners. It is the school’s responsibility to help each child in our care explore their interests. We are proud of how they grow in confidence and develop the resilience to face the challenges ahead of them.

British Values
What are the British values?
All schools are required by law to promote the fundamental British values of:
British values are a set of principles that the Department for Education (DfE) in England expects schools to promote as part of their commitment to students' spiritual, moral, social, and cultural (SMSC) development. These values are meant to prepare pupils for life in modern Britain and include:
democracy
the rule of law
individual liberty
How to Promote British Values
To promote these values effectively, they are integrated into our curriculum and ethos. Here are some ways we do this:

pageCache.text:
Our School Values
Together We Belong, Inspire and Achieve
Every child has the right to an excellent education and deserves to feel valued, safe and successful in school.
Our values guide everything we do:
Through these values, we create a school where everyone feels they belong, is inspired to learn and is empowered to achieve.
Our Aims
Getting You to the Next Level

Welcome
Headteacher's Welcome
Together we belong, inspire and achieve.
Welcome to Bordon Junior School, where every child can be happy and successful.
Thank you for taking time to look through our school website I hope you find it informative and it gives you a feel for our school.
The first years of education are vitally important and choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you will ever make. At Bordon Junior School you will find a learning atmosphere that is happy and stimulating, a curriculum that is exciting, challenging and one that brings learning alive.
Matt Greenhalgh Headteacher
Our school philosophy is to give children the foundations for their future education and the building blocks to succeed in life. We place great importance on children learning the crucial skills of reading, writing and using numbers with confidence. We believe that children need to enjoy their learning in a positive and caring atmosphere to be successful. We all work towards our school values of being confident, being curious, being creative, being respectful, being a team and most importantly, being happy. This helps to ensure that the children in our school are some of the most welcoming you will find.
We are proud to be a part of the University of Chichester Academy Trust. Each of the academies in the University of Chichester Academy Trust has a unique identity, but a shared belief in creating a positive, enriching and inclusive learning environment where all staff and children feel valued.
I hope that, after looking through our website and visiting our school, you will choose us to continue the learning journey you have already started with your child. I very much look forward to working with you on the exciting adventure your child is embarking on and welcoming you to our community.
If you are already one of our parents, and you can not find the information you are searching for, then please come and chat with me and I will help to find what you need.
Matt Greenhalgh Headteacher

Personal Development
At Bordon Infant and Junior Schools, Personal Development is woven throughout school life. Through our curriculum, assemblies, enrichment opportunities, pupil leadership roles, educational visits and wider experiences, pupils develop the knowledge, skills and values needed to thrive in modern Britain.
Our aim is to help children become confident, respectful and responsible individuals who understand how to stay safe, healthy and active, value diversity, build positive relationships and contribute positively to their communities. We want pupils to leave our schools as resilient, independent learners who are well prepared for their next stage of education and life beyond school.

Religious Education
At Bordon Infant and Junior Schools, Religious Education is taught through the Kapow Religion and Worldviews curriculum, which is aligned with the Hampshire Agreed Syllabus. This knowledge-rich curriculum enables pupils to explore a range of religious and non-religious worldviews, helping them to understand how beliefs, values and practices shape the lives of individuals and communities across the world.
Through the study of religion and worldviews, children are encouraged to ask thoughtful questions, engage in respectful discussion and develop an understanding of different perspectives. Pupils learn about a range of faiths and worldviews while reflecting on their own beliefs, experiences and values.
The aims of Religion and Worldviews are to:
Our Religion and Worldviews curriculum helps pupils to become informed, open-minded and reflective individuals who are prepared to live positively in an increasingly diverse society.

Science
At Bordon Junior School, we block our science to allow the children to explore subjects fully and to allow everyone's focus to be on the objectives of the unit.
We are aiming to create inquisitive scientists who are curious about the world around them. Our aim is for everyone to work scientifically and deepen their own learning through experimentation and exploration.
There is clear progression in disciplinary knowledge as pupils learn more about how to work scientifically, see below.

English
At Bordon Junior School, we teach pupils to speak and write fluently so that they can communicate their ideas and emotions to others, and through their reading and listening, others can communicate with them.
Through reading in particular, pupils have a chance to develop culturally, emotionally, intellectually, socially and spiritually. We believe that literature, especially, plays a key role in such development. Reading also enables pupils both to acquire knowledge and to build on what they already know.
For those pupils who need additional help with their reading we follow the Little Wandle letters and sounds phonics scheme. All staff have been trained in delivering this.

Geography
Pupils develop a growing understanding of the wider world including knowing the location of the main countries and capital cities of the U.K., Europe and the Americas.
They need to grasp important geographical concepts such as ‘climate’ and use geographical language such as ‘equator’, ‘latitude’ and ‘hemisphere’. The units are designed to introduce them to increasingly complex aspects of human and physical geography for example, through our unit on Coasts in Year 3 and studying Volcanoes and Earthquakes in Year 6.
Throughout the school, we want immersive experiences for finding out about Geography. We support this with fieldwork visits, for example to Hayling Island in Year 3, through using digital programs such as Google Earth and through challenging activities such as analysing earthquake data in Year 6.
Geography Long Term Plan 26-27

History
At Bordon Infant and Junior Schools, we inspire children to develop a curiosity about the past and an understanding of how history has shaped the world around them. Through engaging enquiries, pupils learn to think and work as historians, asking questions, investigating evidence and developing an understanding of chronology, cause and consequence, change and continuity, similarity and difference, and historical significance.
Our carefully sequenced curriculum enables children to build their historical knowledge progressively from the Early Years through to Year 6. Pupils explore a diverse range of people, events and civilisations while developing the skills needed to analyse, interpret and evaluate historical evidence.
History is brought to life through a variety of enriching experiences, including educational visits, visitors and immersive learning opportunities. These experiences help children make meaningful connections with the past and deepen their understanding of the people, places and events they study.
Through the study of History, we aim to foster a lifelong love of learning about the past. Children develop an appreciation of different societies, cultures and perspectives, helping them to understand both their own heritage and the wider world. By exploring significant events and individuals from local, British and world history, pupils leave Bordon Infant and Junior Schools with the knowledge, skills and curiosity needed to continue their historical learning throughout their lives.

Year 5 visiting Hampton Court Palace as part of their Tudor topic.
History Long Term Plan 2026-27

Mathematics
Our vision for learning mathematics at Bordon Junior School is to develop young mathematicians who use numbers flexibly, explore the ‘big ideas’ of mathematics and who understand they can use maths to solve problems in all aspects of life.
We aim to show children that mathematics is a highly creative discipline where logic, accuracy and the ability to discern patterns and break problems apart are key skills.

Physical Education
At Bordon Infant and Junior Schools, we aim to inspire all pupils to enjoy being active, develop a love of sport and understand the importance of leading healthy, active lifestyles. Through a broad range of physical activities, games and sports, pupils build confidence, resilience, teamwork and respect for others.
Swimming is an important part of our PE curriculum and all pupils have the opportunity to develop their water confidence, swimming technique and water safety knowledge throughout their time at school.
We believe that physical activity is for everyone and strive to provide opportunities for all children to succeed, challenge themselves and achieve their personal best.
Through our PE curriculum, we aim for pupils to:
Demonstrate resilience, teamwork and respect for others.

Design and Technology
At Bordon Infant and Junior Schools, our Design and Technology curriculum encourages children to become creative thinkers and problem-solvers. Through designing, making and evaluating products, pupils develop practical skills and technical knowledge while learning how to create purposeful solutions to real-life challenges.
Skills and knowledge are built progressively throughout the school, enabling children to refine their ideas, learn from experience and improve their work over time. Design and Technology also provides opportunities for pupils to apply learning from across the curriculum, particularly in mathematics, science, computing and art.
Through our DT curriculum, we aim for pupils to:

Apply learning from other curriculum subjects.
